purpose: One pinned PICASO boundary: PICASO (Batalha et al. 2019) owns the radiative transfer of a substellar atmosphere and the intensity it emits at each viewing angle. cssEarth owns the choice of model atmosphere, the passband weighting, the quadratic fit and scientific qualification.
license: PICASO is GPL-3.0 (PICASO-LICENSE.txt, from its 4.1 wheel). Its reference data come with the release. The Sonora Bobcat profiles (Marley et al. 2021) and the PICASO 4.0 correlated-k tables are CC BY 4.0 on Zenodo. NumPy, SciPy, Astropy and pandas are BSD-style.
platform: The lock pins the versions pip resolves on macOS arm64 with Python 3.11; another platform may resolve other versions and needs its own lock.

data.reference: picaso.data.get_reference, the reference folder of the installed release (config.json version 4.1)

profiles.note: Sonora Bobcat (Marley et al. 2021, ApJ 920, 85) cloud-free, solar-metallicity structures, one per temperature and gravity (tTTTTgGGGnc_m0.0.dat, gravity in m/s^2): the release of the paper.

opacities.note: PICASO 4.0 pre-weighted correlated-k tables, 196 spectral windows, the archive with TiO and VO that its authors recommend. The table read is solar metallicity and the solar C/O PICASO itself uses (solar_cto = 0.458 in picaso/justdoit.py), the composition of the Bobcat profiles; a Diamondback model at [M/H] +0.5 reads the +0.5 table at the same C/O. The archive's other 66 tables are not unpacked.

cloudyProfiles.note: Sonora Diamondback (Morley et al. 2024, ApJ 975, 59) cloudy structures, one per temperature, gravity, sedimentation efficiency f_sed and metallicity (tTTTTgGGGfF_mM_co1.0.pt, gravity in m/s^2): the release of the paper.

cloudProperties.note: The same release's cloud optical depth, asymmetry and single-scattering albedo per layer in the 196 spectral windows, one file per structure (300 MB). Kept as the archive; a model's file is unpacked when a law is computed from it.

passband.note: SVO Filter Profile Service, Generic/Bessell.V: the band Howarth (2011) and the color dataset's other V-band laws are computed in.

passbands.note: Any other SVO transmission curve, by its filter id, fetched when a law is first computed in it: the middle band of an imaged planet's infrared color (MKO/NSFCam.H, 2MASS/2MASS.H, JWST/NIRCam.F430M).

why: No published limb-darkening table reaches a brown dwarf or an imaged planet below 1,500 K. PICASO computes the emergent intensity of a published model atmosphere at Gauss angles, from which the law is fitted as the table authors fit theirs: a cloud-free Sonora Bobcat atmosphere for a dwarf, and for an imaged planet the cloudy Sonora Diamondback model a paper fitted to it.
